reason: Before the fix, the JIT fastpass only guards the issues-concat on presence, not the value assignment, so a swallowed issue on an absent optional key still writes its leaked value into the output, meaning "a" in result.data would be true instead of the expected false.
The PR guards both the issues concat and the value assignment on presence, which is exactly the added regression test's expected behavior, so it passes after the fix.

Before the fix, the paragraph continuation lookahead only recognizes space-only lines as blank, so a tab-only separator line gets swallowed as a lazy continuation, merging the two paragraphs into one instead of two.
The fix widens the blank-line lookahead to include tabs ([ \t]+\n), matching the new spec test the PR adds, so two separate paragraphs are produced.
The PR only changes error-path stack decoration in Axios's catch handler; it has no effect on successful JSON response parsing, so this unrelated test passes at the base revision too.
Same reasoning as base: the change is confined to error-path stack handling and does not affect successful JSON response parsing.
The PR only changes the negative-number-exponent regex; boolean flag parsing is unrelated and unaffected at the base revision.
Boolean flag parsing is untouched by the uppercase-E exponent fix, so it passes identically after the PR too.

Before the fix, JsonTreeReader.nextInt() has no ASCII validation and goes straight to Integer.parseInt via getAsInt(), which uses Character.digit and silently accepts full-width Unicode digits as 123 instead of throwing.
The fix adds a validateAscii check before parsing string tokens as int/long in JsonTreeReader, throwing MalformedJsonException for full-width digits, matching the added regression test.
Before the fix, parseSearchPath uses an alphanumeric-only allowlist regex that does not include hyphens, so 'test-db' is split into 'test' and 'db' rather than kept as one schema name.
The fix replaces the allowlist regex with a delimiter blocklist that preserves hyphens and accented characters, so 'test-db' stays a single schema name as the new test data provider expects.

The PR only fixes a buffer-recycling resource leak in ByteBufferUtil.fromStream; it does not touch transformation logic, so the default transform-applies-unless-disabled behavior is unaffected at the base revision.
Same reasoning as base: the ByteBufferUtil fix is unrelated to transformation application, so behavior is unchanged after the PR.

The PR only caches the already-correct allowedSymbolsAndAlphanumerics computation; the PR description states behavior is preserved (370 tests pass, identical violation counts before/after), so the naming-rule allowance test passes at the base revision too.
The caching refactor is explicitly verified to preserve configuration behavior, so the allowed-symbol identifier still passes the naming rule after the change.
The PR only adds a missing <cstdint> include for GCC 15 compilation; it has no bearing on SVG data URI percent-decoding behavior, so this unrelated test's outcome is unaffected at the base revision.
The PR only adds Afrikaans week/weeks locale translations; it has no relation to DST-aware hour-shifting logic, so this unrelated test's pre-existing behavior should be unaffected.
Same as base: the GCC 15 <cstdint> include fix is unrelated to SVG data URI percent-decoding behavior.

The PR only changes Cookie-header directive parsing to merge multiple headers; it does not touch form-urlencoded content decoding, so this unrelated optional-fields decode test is unaffected at the base revision.
Same as base: the cookie-header parsing change is unrelated to form-urlencoded decoding of optional-only types.
The PR only fixes comment/test-variable spelling errors; it does not touch the in-memory filesystem's Remove logic, so the non-empty-directory rejection behavior is unaffected at the base revision.
Same as base: spelling-only changes have no effect on the Remove-non-empty-directory behavior.

The PR only fixes a json_encode() call's argument order in a JSON type test; it is unrelated to schema/index-rename comparison logic, so this unrelated test's outcome should be unaffected at the base revision.
Same reasoning as base: the json_encode() argument fix is unrelated to schema/index comparison logic.

The PR only adds Afrikaans week/weeks locale translations; it has no relation to DST-aware hour-shifting logic, so this unrelated test's pre-existing behavior should be unaffected at the base revision.

The PR fixes a permit leak in CircuitBreakerStateMachine's predicate evaluation; it is a different resilience4j component from the semaphore-based RateLimiter's scheduled refresh logic, so this unrelated test's outcome should be unaffected at the base revision.
Same reasoning as base: the CircuitBreaker permit-leak fix does not touch RateLimiter's refresh scheduling.

The PR fixes an ASI hazard in the prefer-template rule's autofix; it is unrelated to the no-var/prefer-const rule's autofix and hoisting preservation, so this unrelated test's outcome should be unaffected at the base revision.
Same reasoning as base: the prefer-template ASI fix does not touch the no-var rule's autofix behavior for hoisted declarations.

The PR only fixes logformatter_adapter()'s handling of empty/tuple args; it does not touch JOBDIR persistence or sitemap crawl resumption, so this unrelated test's outcome should be unaffected at the base revision.
Same reasoning as base: the log-formatter args fix is unrelated to JOBDIR-based crawl resumption.

The PR only widens --sanitize's bidi-control-character detection; it does not touch the character-wrapping/highlight-width clamping logic exercised by this test, so it should be unaffected at the base revision.
Same reasoning as base: the --sanitize bidi fix is unrelated to wrap/highlight width clamping at narrow terminal widths.

The PR only optimizes the RFC5424 structured-data regex for the syslog parser plugin; it is unrelated to the file output plugin's per-key symlink creation, so this unrelated test's outcome should be unaffected at the base revision.
Same reasoning as base: the syslog parser regex optimization does not touch file-output symlink behavior.

The PR only changes virtual-thread yield-spin behavior in ConcurrentBag's handoff loops; it has no relation to pool-name generation or System properties locking, so this unrelated test's outcome should be unaffected at the base revision.
Same reasoning as base: the virtual-thread spin change is unrelated to pool-name generation locking on system properties.

The PR only fixes ACL key-check parsing for the SORT command's STORE argument; it is unrelated to background-save (BGSAVE) behavior on 32-bit builds, so this unrelated test's outcome should be unaffected at the base revision.
Same reasoning as base: the SORT ACL fix does not touch RDB background-save logic.

The PR only fixes globaldir bookkeeping in nvim_win_set_buf's context switching; it is unrelated to CTRL-A increment handling for large numbers, so this unrelated test's outcome should be unaffected at the base revision.
Same reasoning as base: the CWD/globaldir fix does not touch CTRL-X decrement number-parsing logic.

The PR only fixes a race condition in external file cache block reclamation; it is unrelated to the type-inference behavior of the || operator on arrays and NULL, so this unrelated test's outcome should be unaffected at the base revision.
Same reasoning as base: the file-cache race fix does not touch list_concat/|| type inference.

The PR only fixes ScrollBar's drag-scroll input handling for touchscreens; it is unrelated to RefCounted's NOTIFICATION_PREDELETE lifecycle behavior, so this unrelated test's outcome should be unaffected at the base revision.
Same reasoning as base: the ScrollBar input-handling fix does not touch RefCounted notification/destruction behavior.

The PR only adds a validation error for categorical features combined with criterion='absolute_error' in DecisionTreeRegressor; it is unrelated to feature_selection.f_regression's handling of constant columns, so this unrelated test's outcome should be unaffected at the base revision.
Same reasoning as base: the DecisionTreeRegressor categorical-feature validation change does not touch r_regression's correlation computation.

The PR only fixes a readonly-attribute bug in the Swagger UI addon's form fields; it is unrelated to Vault Agent's file sink permission mode, so this unrelated test's outcome should be unaffected at the base revision.
Same reasoning as base: the Swagger UI fix does not touch file sink mode handling.
Before the fix, write_usage's wrap_text("", initial_indent=usage_prefix) call discards the prefix entirely when args is empty, so --help emits a blank first line instead of 'Usage: cli'.
The fix adds an explicit early return that writes the stripped usage_prefix when args is empty, producing 'Usage: cli' as the new regression test verifies.

The PR only fixes .partition(":") usage for IPv6 addresses in the dev server and test client; it is unrelated to Flask's dict-to-JSON response conversion, so this unrelated test's outcome should be unaffected at the base revision.
Same reasoning as base: the IPv6 host-parsing fix does not touch dict-to-JSON response handling.

The PR only fixes an unhashable-generic-alias lookup during core schema generation; it is unrelated to required-field validation on model construction, so this unrelated test's outcome should be unaffected at the base revision.
Same reasoning as base: the schema-generation fix does not touch required-field missing validation.

logging.WARN and logging.WARNING are the same numeric constant (30) in Python's stdlib logging module, so replacing one alias with the other is purely cosmetic and does not change the effective log level or echo suppression behavior at either revision.
Same reasoning as base: WARN/WARNING are identical constants, so echo-flag log suppression behavior is unchanged after the PR.

Once attribute methods are generated, subsequent reads dispatch directly to the generated methods rather than through method_missing, so this steady-state performance benchmark is not affected by the PR's thread-safety fix to the one-time method_missing/definition path.
Same reasoning as base: the thread-safety fix only changes the one-time attribute-method generation path via method_missing, not steady-state attribute access performance.

Before the fix, preProcess() creates a fresh WrappedListener object per dispatch and postProcess only removes not-called wrappers from callStack, so two dispatches of the same event with a called listener leave two distinct wrapper entries in callStack, giving getCalledListeners() two entries as expected.

The fix's new aggregation deduplicates by original listener via in_array() per requestHash/eventName before appending to calledListenerInfos, so dispatching the same event twice with the same listener registered now records only one entry instead of two, breaking the one-entry-per-invocation expectation.

The PR only fixes shellcheck warnings (replacing command substitution with a read loop for COMPREPLY population, and adding a safe '|| return' after pushd/popd) without changing which subcommand's custom completion function is invoked, so this unrelated test's outcome should be unaffected at the base revision.
Same reasoning as base: the shellcheck-driven refactor preserves COMPREPLY population semantics and does not affect per-subcommand completion routing.

qs's arrayLimit (default 20) only affects bracket-indexed keys like a[0]..a[25]; a simple repeated non-indexed key like ids=1&ids=2&...&ids=25 is combined into an array regardless of count in both qs 6.13.0 and 6.14.0, so this test should be unaffected by the dependency bump at the base revision.
Same reasoning as base: the qs version bump does not change how simple repeated non-indexed query keys are parsed into arrays.
Before the fix, get_environ_proxies has the signature def get_environ_proxies(url): with no second parameter, so calling it with only a URL argument works fine.

After the fix, get_environ_proxies is redefined as def get_environ_proxies(url, no_proxy): with no default value for no_proxy, so calling it with only a URL argument now raises TypeError: missing required positional argument 'no_proxy'.
Before the fix, parse_unit_value's gate only accepted digit-leading or '-digit'-leading byte sequences, so '.foons' never entered unit parsing and fell through to normal bareword/string parsing.

The fix widens the gate to also accept a leading '.', so '.foons' now enters parse_unit_value's number/unit matching path; since 'foons' has no digits immediately after the dot, this could produce a parse error instead of falling back to bareword/string parsing as before -- and the PR description itself notes a related, still-unfixed edge case in this same area.

Before the fix, CurlFactory always connects a sink/write-function even for HEAD requests, which is the exact scenario the referenced issue discussion (#2741) reports as failing when combined with an Accept-Encoding header on a HEAD request.

The fix explicitly skips connecting a sink/write-function for HEAD requests, resolving the failure combined with Accept-Encoding, matching the updated regression test that now expects CURLOPT_FILE/CURLOPT_WRITEFUNCTION to be absent for HEAD requests.

The PR only fixes formatting of inserted/deleted maps within list equality diffs; it does not change how match-failure diffs handle improper lists nested inside a map value, so this unrelated crash-avoidance test's outcome should be unaffected at the base revision.
Same reasoning as base: the maps-in-lists formatting fix does not touch improper-list handling in match-failure diffs.

Before the fix, dynamic components handled css_props hydration differently (hydration_node set via next_sibling in $.component vs first_child in $.css_props), causing a hydration mismatch/crash for nested dynamically-selected components with scoped CSS custom properties, exactly the bug issue #16115 and this PR's test target.

The fix unifies how dynamic Component nodes are built (removing the separate $$component branch and its inconsistent anchor handling) and removes the stale css_props teardown, resolving the hydration mismatch, matching the PR's own new runtime-browser test which asserts the color stays red before and after the toggle.

Before this refactor, the plugin's quick prefilter used simple string includes() checks and the actual matching regex used \s* (which matches newlines), so a multi-line new URL(...) call was still detected and transformed correctly.

The refactor adds a rolldown hook filter with code regex /new\s+URL.+import\.meta\.url/ where '.' does not match newlines by default, so a multi-line new URL(...) call (with a newline between the path and import.meta.url) fails this fast prefilter and the transform handler never runs, leaving the asset unbundled.

Before the fix, no FZF_CURRENT_ITEM env var is exported, so a NUL-delimited item's raw text is never placed into the child process's environment, avoiding any NUL-in-env-value issue for the preview command.

The fix unconditionally exports FZF_CURRENT_ITEM=<item text> to the preview child process; when --delimiter=$'\0' is used the item's raw text itself contains embedded NUL bytes, and POSIX/Go environment variables cannot contain NUL bytes, so setting up the child process's environment is likely to fail exactly for this NUL-delimited scenario.

This is the exact scenario (immersiveSticky -> edgeToEdge not properly restoring system bars) that issue #165328 and this PR describe as broken under the old deprecated View.SYSTEM_UI_FLAG_* approach, which this PR was specifically written to fix.

The fix introduces isEdgeToEdge state tracking and enableEdgeToEdge()/disableEdgeToEdge() using WindowCompat, explicitly restoring the system bars when transitioning into edgeToEdge mode from other modes like immersiveSticky, matching the PR's stated purpose and new tests.
Before this PR, no MultipleCaseAssignment check exists in the semantic syntax checker, so a class pattern like ClassLabel(num_classes=num_classes) is not flagged at all.

For a MatchClass keyword like num_classes=num_classes, the visitor calls self.insert(&keyword.attr) (inserting the attribute name 'num_classes') and then self.visit_pattern(&keyword.pattern), which for a bare capture pattern also inserts the same name 'num_classes' via the MatchAs branch; since the HashSet already contains it, this incorrectly triggers a 'multiple assignments to name' syntax error for this valid, common shorthand pattern.

Before the fix, decodeBodyToStruct assumes the destination slice already has enough capacity and indexes sli.Index(i) without growing it, so decoding two blocks into a pre-populated slice of length 1 panics with an index-out-of-range error at i=1.
The fix appends a new zero value to the slice whenever i >= sli.Len(), matching the new regression test which expects both blocks decoded without panicking.

Before the fix, mockConstructorParameters only calls setTimezone when an explicit $timezone argument is passed; when Carbon::setTestNow() is called with just a Carbon instance (no explicit timezone), the mocked 'now' keeps the LA timezone it was constructed with instead of falling back to the application's default UTC timezone.

The fix changes the condition to always set the timezone via $timezone ?? date_default_timezone_get() whenever the test instance is a DateTimeInterface, so an untimezoned mock now falls back to the default UTC timezone, matching the new testTimezoneConsistency test.

Before the fix, PROTOCOL_RELATIVE_REGEX = /^[/\\]{2}[^/\\]+/ requires exactly two leading slashes followed immediately by a non-slash character, so '///test.com' (a third leading slash) fails to match and is not classified as protocol-relative, and mixed/whitespace-separated slash patterns are likewise rejected.
The fix widens the regex to /^([/\\]\s*){2,}[^/\\]/, allowing two or more leading slashes with optional whitespace between them, matching all three new test cases as protocol-relative.

The PR only changes the internal byte-array accessor used by combineOrdered/combineUnordered as a performance micro-optimization with no value change; it does not touch the MD5 hash function itself, so this unrelated test's outcome should be unaffected at the base revision.
Same reasoning as base: the internal accessor swap for hash-combining does not affect MD5 digest computation.

The PR is a pure code-organization refactor that moves diagnostic descriptors into a dedicated class without changing diagnostic codes, messages, severities, or the client-generation logic itself, so the generated GET client continues to work identically at the base revision.
Same reasoning as base: moving diagnostics into a separate class is a no-op refactor with respect to generated client behavior.

The PR explicitly removes only redundant trailing 'continue' statements that were already the last thing each loop iteration would do, with no change in control flow, so basic HTTP/1.1 response fetching is unaffected at the base revision.
Same reasoning as base: removing redundant continue statements with explicitly no control-flow change does not affect basic response body fetching.
Before the fix, to_iso8601/2 converts the date to Calendar.ISO and then calls to_iso8601() with no format argument, discarding the requested :basic format and always returning the extended form.

The fix passes the requested format through to_iso8601(format) after converting to Calendar.ISO, so a Holocene-calendar date now correctly renders as '20010101' in basic format, matching the new regression test.

Before the fix, setEndDate() updates the internal endDate state but never re-syncs the native PHP 8.2+ DatePeriod 'end' property, so both ->end and getEndDate() would still report or be inconsistent with the original construction-time end date.

The fix adds syncNativePeriod(), which reinitializes the parent DatePeriod via parent::__construct after setEndDate()/setStartDate(), correctly updating the native 'end' property, matching the new regression test.

Before the fix, headline() builds the request URI without checking for embedded whitespace, so a custom normalizer that passes a newline-containing path through unchanged would be transmitted as-is rather than raising an error.
The fix adds a request_uri.match?(/\s/) check that raises HTTP::RequestError before sending, exactly matching the new regression spec for a newline-containing path from a passthrough normalizer.

The PR only adds a pluralName ('milionë') to the Albanian locale data; it does not touch the English locale's million pluralization, so this unrelated test's outcome should be unaffected at the base revision.
Same reasoning as base: the Albanian-only locale fix has no effect on English number-to-words output.

The PR only changes how non-String Properties entries are filtered during environment property loading; a module with no custom properties involved is unaffected by this change, so basic singleton resolution should work the same at the base revision.
Same reasoning as base: the properties ClassCastException fix does not touch singleton scope resolution.

The PR description explicitly states this is a behavior-preserving refactor extracting a shared _replaceNew primitive with no public API change, and that the existing test suite passes unmodified, so replaceElement's ordering and duplicate-key behavior is unaffected at the base revision.
Same reasoning as base: the shared-primitive refactor is explicitly behavior-preserving, so replaceElement continues to work identically after the PR.

The PR is a pure refactor replacing a manual 'if size < 0 { size = 0 }' check with the equivalent built-in max(size, 0) call, with no behavioral difference, so parsing '-5MB' still yields 0 at the base revision.
Same reasoning as base: max(cast.ToInt(sizeStr), 0) is behaviorally identical to the prior manual clamp.

Before the fix, findCaseInsensitivePathRec always takes n.children[0] when wildChild is true, but addChild() appends the wildcard child at the end of the array, so a node with both a static child (xxx) and a wildcard child (:id) picks the static node first and the switch on n.nType falls into the default case and panics for the mis-cased or unmatched request.

The fix tries static children via indices first and falls back to n.children[len(n.children)-1] for the wildcard child (matching getValue()'s existing behavior), resolving the mis-cased static route and returning a plain not-found for the unmatched path without panicking, as the new regression tests verify.
Before the fix, toBigInt() returns n.Int unchanged when Exp is 0, so for a Numeric{Valid: true} with a nil Int field, Int64Value's call to IsInt64 dereferences the nil *big.Int and panics.

The fix adds a nil check at the top of toBigInt() that returns big.NewInt(0) when n.Int is nil, so Int64Value now returns zero instead of panicking, matching the new TestNumericInt64Valuer case for pgtype.Numeric{Valid: true}.

The PR only fixes tab-stop restoration in the renderer when hard tabs are enabled; it is unrelated to the Program's quit/shutdown handling from an external goroutine, so this unrelated test's outcome should be unaffected at the base revision.
Same reasoning as base: the renderer tab-stop fix does not touch Program.Quit()/run-loop shutdown logic.

Before the fix, run_until_cancelled always constructs and awaits RunUntilCancelledFuture without first checking is_cancelled(), so on an already-cancelled token the wrapped future can still be polled -- for a future that panics on its first poll, this causes the test to panic instead of returning None immediately.

The fix adds an explicit self.is_cancelled() check that returns None before ever constructing/polling the wrapped future when the token is already cancelled, matching the new regression test that panics if the future is ever polled.

The PR only optimizes skipping unreachable ignore-file loading (performance, no change to parallel traversal or content matching); it is unrelated to case-insensitive pattern matching within file contents, so this unrelated test's outcome should be unaffected at the base revision.
Same reasoning as base: the ignore-file-loading optimization does not touch case-insensitive content search matching.

The nested 'if let Default::None = *container_default { if skip_deserializing... }' is logically equivalent to the flattened 'if container_default.is_none() && skip_deserializing...' -- this is purely a denesting refactor, so a skip_deserializing field with no custom default still defaults via Default::Default at the base revision.
Same reasoning as base: the flattened condition preserves the exact same logic, so the skipped field still receives its type's default value after the PR.
